posts.caption:
Your TFSA room could be $109,000.

If you were 18 or older in 2009 and have lived in Canada since, every year's limit has added up: $109,000 by 2026.
Watch it build: $5,000 in 2009, $41,000 by 2015, $69,500 by 2020, $109,000 by 2026. Unused room never expires. It just waits for you.

Why it matters: every dollar of growth inside a TFSA is tax-free, forever, even when you take it out.

Now watch it grow. Fill it with $7,000 a year from age 30, growing 10% a year:
At 40: about $111,562
At 50: about $400,925
At 60: about $1,151,458
All of it tax-free. Can't do $7,000? Any amount grows the same way, just smaller.

The part nobody tells you: put in more than your room, and the CRA charges 1% a month on the extra, every month it stays in.

Your room in 5 minutes:
1. Log in to CRA My Account.
2. Find "TFSA room". It's your room as of January 1.
3. Subtract anything you've already put in this year. That's what you can still add.

The mindset: The Simple Path to Wealth's big idea is to use every tax shelter you're given, then let it sit. The TFSA is Canada's best one for most people.

Do this: before your next deposit, check your TFSA room in CRA My Account.

The rule to remember: room unused is growth unclaimed.

Money Foundations, Part 7. Tonight at 7: the withdrawal trap.

Send this to the friend who just opened a TFSA.

Not guaranteed. Returns vary.

#TFSA #personalfinancecanada #CRA #investingcanada #moneyfoundations
posts.first_comment: Sources: CRA TFSA dollar limits 2009 to 2026 (total $109,000 if you were 18 or older and a resident of Canada since 2009); TD, 'TFSA contribution room and withdrawal rules': withdrawals are added back to your room the following year (January 1); over-contributions are taxed 1% per month on the highest excess amount, for every month it stays in. Your exact room is in CRA My Account (as of January 1, so subtract this year's deposits). Education, not tax advice. Maths: cumulative room = the sum of each year's CRA limit. $7,000 at the end of each year, compounded yearly at 10% a year, no fees: ≈ $111,562 after 10 years, $400,925 after 20, $1,151,458 after 30 (contribution room is indexed to inflation in $500 steps, so future limits may be higher). 10% = the S&P 500's long-run average (Fidelity), before inflation. Ideas: J.L. Collins, The Simple Path to Wealth.

posts.caption:
Felt like you did nothing this week? You probably did more than you think. You just can't see it.

THE STUDY: Harvard researchers had 238 people at 7 companies write a short diary every workday, about 12,000 entries in all. On people's best days, one thing showed up far more than anything else: making progress on work that mattered, even a small win. On their worst days: setbacks.

WHY YOU FEEL BEHIND: a to-do list only shows what's left, and it never ends. Four Thousand Weeks makes the point bluntly: you will never get to the bottom of it. So if the list is your scoreboard, you lose every day. A done list shows how far you came.

THE DONE LIST:
1. Every evening, 2 minutes. Same notebook, same spot (next to the laptop, by the kettle).
2. Write 3 things you moved forward. Finished or not.
3. Small counts: "sent the quote", "fixed one bug", "called Mom back", "10 minutes on the budget".
4. Friday: read the week's page before you plan next week.

BAD-DAY RESCUE: when you feel behind, read last week's list before you open this week's to-do list. Proof beats feelings.

WHAT CHANGES: Day 1, three lines. Week 1, 15 wins you would have forgotten by Saturday. Year 1, a notebook full of proof that you're moving.

The rule that stays: count what moved, not what's left.

Do this: tonight, write down 3 things you moved forward this week. Small ones count. Then do it every evening.

Send this to the friend who feels behind.

#productivity #motivation #worklife #focus #smallwins
posts.first_comment: Source: Amabile & Kramer, The Progress Principle (Harvard Business Review Press, 2011) and HBS Working Knowledge: 238 people at 7 companies filled in about 12,000 daily diaries; making progress in meaningful work, even a small win, was by far the most common event on people's best days, and setbacks on their worst. Burkeman, O. (2021), Four Thousand Weeks (keep a 'done list').

posts.caption:
Putting TFSA money back? Wait. Here's the trap.

You take out $5,000 in March and put it back in June. Feels harmless. But the room from a withdrawal only comes back on January 1 of the next year. If you had no other room left, that $5,000 is an over-contribution, and the CRA charges 1% a month on it until it's out: $50 a month, about $350 from June to December.

Do this: before you put money back, check your room in CRA My Account (it shows your room as of January 1). Moving money between banks? Ask for a direct transfer, which doesn't count as a withdrawal.

Already did it? Take the extra out as soon as you can, and look up form RC243 (the TFSA return) on canada.ca.

The rule to remember: took it out this year? Put it back on or after January 1.

Send this to your TFSA friend.

Follow for one money move a day, in plain words.

#TFSA #personalfinancecanada #CRA #taxtips #moneyfoundations
posts.first_comment: Sources: CRA (canada.ca), 'Before you contribute to a TFSA' and the TFSA withdrawal pages: withdrawals are added back to your contribution room at the beginning of the following year; an excess amount is taxed 1% per month for each month it stays in the account; direct transfers between your own TFSAs are not withdrawals; excess amounts are reported on form RC243. Your room as of January 1 is in CRA My Account (subtract this year's deposits). Maths: 1% of $5,000 = $50 for each month the excess stays in; June through December = 7 months = $350. Education, not tax advice.

posts.caption:
Paid Friday. Broke by Wednesday? The habit: pay yourself first.

Rich Habits, Decoded No. 1. Each episode takes one money habit and shows you how to do it on a normal paycheque.

WHAT IT MEANS: savings come out the day your pay lands, automatically, before you can spend it. You live on what's left, instead of saving what's left.

WHY IT WORKS: you don't rely on willpower. In the 'Save More Tomorrow' study, workers who signed up to save automatically, with the rate rising at each raise, went from saving 3.5% of pay to 13.6% over 40 months.

HOW TO DO IT (10 minutes in your banking app):
1. Open a separate savings account (ideally one that pays interest and that you don't see every day).
2. Set an automatic transfer for payday. Start at 10%; if that's too much, start at 1% or 2%.
3. Every raise: add 1 percentage point.
4. Leave it. The point is not having to decide again.

THE CATCH: if you carry card debt at 20%+, point the automatic payment at that first. Keep a small buffer so the transfer never bounces.

Do this: set one automatic transfer for your next payday, even if it's $10.

Rich Habits, Decoded No. 2 is Wednesday at 5 pm.

Education only, not financial advice.

Follow for one money move a day, in plain words.

#personalfinance #savingmoney #payyourselffirst #moneytips #richhabits

posts.caption:
It's 3 am. You're feeding. Your eyes keep closing.

3 am Club No. 1: where you feed matters most on the nights you're running on empty.

THE RULE: falling asleep with your baby on a sofa or armchair is one of the riskiest places to doze off together. If there's any chance you'll nod off, move before you sit down.

SET UP YOUR 3 AM SPOT BEFORE BED (5 minutes):
1. Pick the spot now, while you're awake: never the sofa or armchair. Safest is baby back in their own crib beside you.
2. If you feed in bed and might doze, keep pillows and duvets away from baby.
3. Baby's own sleep space (crib or bassinet, flat, firm, empty) within arm's reach.
4. Water, a dim light and your phone charger by the spot, so you don't end up on the sofa.
5. After the feed, baby goes back in their own space, on their back.

THE CATCH: no spot is risk-free if you've been drinking, smoke, or take medicine that makes you drowsy, or if your baby was premature or low birth weight. Then baby sleeps in their own space only.

Do this: tonight, set up your 3 am spot before you go to bed.

3 am Club No. 2 is Wednesday at 5 pm: what to do when the baby is wide awake at 3 am.

Follow for one calm thing a night, from bump to toddler.

General information only, not medical advice.

#newborn #nightfeeds #safesleep #newparents #3amclub
posts.first_comment: Sources: NHS, 'Sudden infant death syndrome (SIDS)': do not sleep on a sofa or armchair with your baby; put baby on their back in their own cot or Moses basket. The Lullaby Trust, 'Safer sleep advice': if you think you might fall asleep while feeding, it is safer to do so in an adult bed clear of pillows and duvets than on a sofa or armchair; risk is much higher after alcohol, drugs or smoking. Government of Canada, 'Safe sleep for your baby': avoid sleeping with your baby on a sofa, armchair or couch; baby sleeps on their back in a crib, cradle or bassinet.

posts.caption:
AI's answer felt generic again? Add one line: "Before you answer, ask me 3 questions."

AI, for real · Day 8. One real test of what AI can do, with the output shown.

WHY IT WORKS: a chatbot fills every gap in your request with the most average guess. Asking it to question you first makes it name the gaps, and you fill them with your real details.

THE REAL TEST:
Request (made up): "Plan a birthday dinner for 6 people, $150 budget. Before you answer, ask me 3 questions."

The AI's reply (Claude, by Anthropic, run Oct 22, 2026), the 3 questions as asked; each came with a line on why it matters:
"Before I plan the birthday dinner, I have 3 questions:
1. Dining out or cooking at home?
2. Any dietary restrictions, allergies, or cuisine preferences in the group?
3. Does the $150 need to cover everything, or only food?"
Then: "Once you answer, I'll build the full plan: menu or restaurant shortlist, itemized budget, timeline, and shopping or booking list."

Answer those 3, and the plan you get is yours, not a generic one.

WHERE IT HELPS: trip plans, cover letters, meal plans, gift ideas, anything where "it depends".

PRIVACY TIP: answer the questions without full names, addresses or account numbers. "My sister" works fine.

Do this: next time you ask AI for a plan, end with "Before you answer, ask me 3 questions."

AI, for real · Day 9 is Wednesday at 5:45 pm.

That sparkle button? It's AI. You already use it every day.

Meta says about a billion people use Meta AI every month, mostly inside WhatsApp, Instagram, Facebook and Messenger. On newer iPhones, Apple Intelligence adds Writing Tools to almost every text box. In Gmail, Gemini can summarise long threads.

Why: big tech isn't waiting for you to visit an AI website. It's putting AI where you already are, so the button is often right there and easy to scroll past.

Do this: tap the ✦ once today, on one real task. Then check what it says.
